Posted May 6, 2003
Analysis By Richard Cowan
As the press releases below explain, next week, Health Canada's Office of Cannabis Medical Access' (OCMA) Stakeholder Advisory Committee will hear from representatives of the groups that really do have a stake in medical cannabis, the patients and their providers. Amazingly, the patients - 'exemptees' and 'licencees' have never been directly consulted during this advisory process.

That's right. Those most directly involved are not considered stakeholders by Health Canada.

But if they are not, then who are the stakeholders from Ann McLellan's perspective?

The list is below, and as you will see, it includes some good groups, but it also includes five representatives from almost every aspect of law enforcement. More absurdly, it has a representative of the so-called Physicians for a Smoke-Free Canada, whose only stake in the issue is their opposition to any smoking of cannabis, no matter how brief or badly needed. Of course, they never mention vaporization. Last year, they sent Ann McLellan a brownie recipe as a publicity stunt.

Then there is the Canadian Medical Association

It would seem to make sense for such a group to be included. However, they have performed very badly in dealing with medical cannabis. In fairness, they have their moments.
See
 Journal of Canadian Medical Association Calls for Decriminalization. Perfect Timing. Contrast with DEAland.

And Health Canada's now moribund system that was supposedly going to provide cannabis to patients, put doctors in an impossible situation, but they have made a bad situation much worse, as you can see from the following link, as well as their own publications, linked in the Stakeholders membership list below.
See
 Cruelty, Incompetence, And Quackery Threaten Canadian Medical Cannabis Patients.

It is quite clear that Health Canada considers the needs of the patients secondary to the need to maintain cannabis prohibition. It could not exclude powerful groups like the Canadian Aids Society or the Arthritis Society, which are generally in favor of medical access to cannabis. However, they have no expertise on the subject.

In fact, it would appear that avoiding those with actual knowledge is more important than avoiding those who support medical access on general principles. That sounds strange, I realize, but this is cannabis, and knowledge about it is dangerous. It makes people think about what is really going on, and no one at Health Canada wants that to happen to them.
See
 Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: Monday, May 5, 2003.
Reference Link: http://www.medicalmarihuana.ca/meeting.html

On May 12, 2003, Canada's largest group of legal cannabis users and growers will present their demands to Health Canada at a meeting in Montreal. It will be at the Office of Cannabis Medical Access' (OCMA) Stakeholder Advisory Committee meeting at the Delta Centre Ville (777 University Street) on the 12th and 13th of May starting at 9am. The presentation will be conducted in the Versaille Room.

The OCMA Advisory Committee was formed in the fall of 2002 with the intent of proposing changes to the MMAR. Unfortunately, the patients - 'exemptees' and 'licencees' have never been directly consulted during this advisory process.

This is the third time that the committee has met, and it is the second meeting since Honourable Ontario Superior Court Justice Sidney Lederman declared the Health Canada program unconstitutional for only giving the " illusion of access " to medicinal cannabis. Health Canada has until July 9th to put a distribution system in place, otherwise the federal laws concerning the personal possession of cannabis will be struck down.

Health Canada's Stakeholder Advisory Committee (SAC) will be given a list of demands and concerns during the May 12th meeting by a group of patients from across Canada. The group, called the 'Medusers', would like Health Canada to address the following concerns and demands to make the program more effective and relevant:

1. Inclusion of 2 permanent representatives on the Stakeholder Advisory Committee, nominated and elected by the exemptees and licencees in the OCMA program.
2. Begin immediate distribution of the PPS cannabis to exemptees.
3. Immediate removal of the overly burdensome registration and renewal requirements.
4. Legal amnesty for all legitimate users, growers and distributors of medicinal cannabis.
5. Financial restitution to cover the cost of therapeutic cannabis.
6. The immediate addressing of the Lederman/Hitszig decision and it's consequences on the program.
See
 Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.
and links

" The courts have said that this program is unconstitutional. Health Canada has yet to address the very urgent needs of the 1000 Canadians signed up under the MMAR (Marijuana Medical Access Regulations) " says Philippe Lucas, an elected representative for the Medusers group. " In over 3 years and millions of taxpayer dollars spent on the OCMA, Health Canada has never supplied a gram, joint or seed to a single suffering Canadian. It is time for Health Canada and Minister McLellan to live up to the compassionate nature of the program by implementing the immediate distribution of the Prairie Plant Systems cannabis, rather than forcing critically and chronically ill Canadians onto the streets to access their medicine. "

The Vancouver Island Compassion Society

For Immediate Press Attention
Local Medicinal Cannabis Expert to Address Health Canada Advisory Committee

Philippe Lucas, founder and director of the Vancouver Island Compassion Society (www.thevics.com) will be joining Hilary Black of the British Columbia Compassion Club Society (www.thecompassionclub.org) in addressing the Health Canada Office of Cannabis Medical Access Advisory Committee on behalf of Canada's compassion clubs and societies.

I m really looking forward to this opportunity, said Lucas, who last year presented to the Senate Special
Committee On Illegal Drugs and was the Victoria Green Party candidate during the 2002 municipal elections.

The Health Canada program is completely unworkable in February it was actually found unconstitutional for only presenting the illusion of access. ". The VICS has been helping critically and chronically ill Canadians gain access to a safe supply of cannabis for over 3 years now; we look forward to sharing our considerable experience and concerns.

Asked what he plans to discuss at the meeting, Lucas mentions that the VICS is currently involved in more therapeutic cannabis research than even Health Canada: We're currently finishing a hepatitis-C survey protocol with the University of California, San Francisco, and we're just about to start research into cannabis use and nausea with UVic and UBC. We have a unique and extensive knowledge of therapeutic cannabis and we look forward to sharing this information.

The Advisory Committee gathers every three months and is charged with advising Health Canada in regards to the Medical Marijuana Access Regulations (MMAR); the upcoming meeting will be taking place on May 12th in Montreal.
